text:
PagerDuty Bot: ALERT: paging oncall for HIGH tail latency for customer: 'harbor-fin'. p95 420ms -> 1.9s, p99 1.8s -> 6.4s, streaming stalls observed. Incident ID: INC-20260314-89

alice.sre: acked. I'm oncall. Seeing paging; assigning triage. Initial hypothesis: single-tenant traffic surge + long prefixes causing KV cache thrash on the dedicated pool.

ben.infra: data from metrics: their qps jumped x4 at 14:02 UTC, concurrent streams up from 60 -> 240. Autoscaler didn't trigger fast enough because connections are sticky.

carla.ml: can you post model + route? could be large-context Llama-2 variant with long prefix. That model has higher KV cache pressure.

alice.sre: route: /v1/generate (model: open-llm/l2-34b-dense, variant: q4_0), tenant: harbor-fin (single-tenant pool group id: st-27).

alice.sre: quick checks in cluster:
```bash
# tail -n 200 logs for pool st-27
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/st-27-runtime -c runtime | grep "kvcache" | tail -n 50
```

k8s-bot: recent logs show repeated evict/rehydrate cycles: "KVCache miss, evicting oldest prefix" ~3000x in last 10m.

ben.infra: heapster / node metrics: GPU memory stable, CPU jitter high on runtime pods 0/3 due to GOMAXPROCS spikes. This aligns with batch/queue contention.

dave.support: customer reports streaming chops/stalls to users. They've escalated internal SLAs. Impact: two core product flows affected (invoice generation, live Q&A).

carla.ml: I pulled a sample of their prompts via the debug buffer. Many requests have ~12k token prefixes (legal docs pasted), then short followups. That explains repeated KV cache churn and high p99.

alice.sre: mitigation plan (fast): 1) divert new traffic for harbor-fin to a fallback lighter model (l2-13b) with faster KV footprint; 2) enable aggressive prefix caching (increase prefix window) for this pool; 3) temporarily limit concurrency per-connection.

ben.infra: implementing 1) now: updating routing rule to route harbor-fin -> st-27-fallback (l2-13b) for POST /v1/generate. Applying canary to 10% then 100%.

ben.infra: command:
```bash
# update routing policy
redwoodctl routes set --tenant st-27 --route generate --model open-llm/l2-13b-dense --canary 10
```

alice.sre: Also increasing runtime prefix retention param on st-27 pods. Patch config: 
```yaml
kv_cache:
  retention_tokens: 65536  # was 16384
  eviction_policy: lru_windowed
```
rolling restart after config apply.

k8s-bot: rolling restart started for deployment st-27-runtime (3 pods). Pod 1 restarted at 14:18 UTC.

carla.ml: note: fallback will reduce output quality for some cases. We'll route partial traffic only until stability. Also preparing quick eval of quality delta on a sample of 50 prompts.

alice.sre: live telemetry: within 6 minutes of 10% canary, p99 dropped from 6.4s -> 2.1s; within 12 minutes after full switch p99 at 1.1s, streaming stall counts down 86%. p95 back to ~380ms.

dave.support: updating customer via ticket: laid out mitigation and expected temporary quality delta. Asked to inform if they want to throttle workload source.

ben.infra: follow-up: autoscaler tweak to consider connection-surge signals (not just CPU) tracked as ENGINF-442. I'll open PR after stabilization.

alice.sre: still seeing intermittent stalls for older in-flight sessions that didn't migrate. Doing targeted pod drains to force reconnection.

carla.ml: analysis: root cause = long-prefix heavy load combined with KV cache eviction oscillation + sticky connections preventing auto-scaling reaction; model variant q4_0 on l2-34b has large per-session state.

alice.sre: post-mitigation next steps:
- keep harbor-fin on fallback for 2 hours while we monitor
- prepare config to increase KV cache retention on dedicated pools for large-context customers
- add rate-limiting knob per-tenant to smooth rapid surges
- plan a workload-specific onboarding doc for customers with >8k prefix patterns

ben.infra: created ticket INFRA-1987: "Connection surge autoscaler metric" with initial design notes.

dave.support: customer accepted mitigation, wants postmortem and recommended long-term config. Notified account team.

alice.sre: handing off to next oncall (ben.infra takes P1 watch). Monitoring window until 16:30 UTC. If anything regresses ping @oncall-rotation.

oncall-rotation: acknowledged. I have runbook link and will watch dashboards.

carla.ml: I'll run offline eval and drop a short list of model + quantization alternatives (13b q4 vs 34b q2) with expected token-cost delta.

alice.sre: adding notes to incident tracker: INC-20260314-89, severity: high, impact: single-tenant SLO breach (p99), mitigation: routing to fallback model + kv_cache retention bump, root cause: long-prefix-induced KV cache thrash + sticky conn + autoscaler gap.

alice.sre: closing on-call thread. Will file full postmortem after 24h data. :white_check_mark:
